versions.source: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual 8th Edition / NCCN / UICC
versions.provenance: 8th edition staging, verified against AJCC 8th edition / NCCN guidelines; licensed verification standard. Requires R1 clinical verification before unchecked use.
versions.introduction: Hypopharyngeal SCC (pyriform sinus most common, then postcricoid and posterior pharyngeal wall) presents late with submucosal spread and a rich lymphatic network, so nodal disease is frequent and often bilateral. T1 tumours are limited to one subsite and 2 cm or smaller; fixation of the hemilarynx or extension to oesophageal mucosa upstages to T3; thyroid/cricoid cartilage destruction and central-compartment soft-tissue invasion define T4a. Nodal staging follows the head-and-neck ENE scheme.

t.label: Tumour limited to one subsite of the hypopharynx and 2 cm or smaller
Tumour invades more than one subsite or an adjacent site, or measures larger than 2 cm up to 4 cm, without hemilarynx fixation
Tumour larger than 4 cm, or with fixation of the hemilarynx, or extension to oesophageal mucosa
Moderately advanced: invasion of thyroid or cricoid cartilage, hyoid bone, thyroid gland, oesophageal musculature, or central-compartment soft tissue
Very advanced: invasion of prevertebral fascia, encasement of carotid artery, or mediastinal structures

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
Single ipsilateral node 3 cm or smaller, extranodal extension negative (ENE-)
Single ipsilateral node larger than 3 cm up to 6 cm, ENE-
Multiple ipsilateral nodes 6 cm or smaller, ENE-
Bilateral or contralateral nodes 6 cm or smaller, ENE-
Any node larger than 6 cm, ENE-
Any node with clinically overt extranodal extension (ENE+)

versions.regionalNodes: Levels II, III and IV jugular nodes plus retropharyngeal and paratracheal (level VI) nodes; bilateral drainage is common, and postcricoid lesions drain to paratracheal nodes. Contralateral or bilateral nodes upstage to N2c.
versions.histologicGrade: Well differentiated (G1), moderately differentiated (G2), poorly differentiated (G3); submucosal spread beyond visible margins is characteristic and reported with margin status.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Conventional squamous cell carcinoma (vast majority); basaloid and spindle-cell variants; postcricoid tumours associated with Plummer-Vinson (iron-deficiency) background.
prognosticFactors: Subsite (pyriform sinus vs postcricoid vs posterior wall)
Nutritional and airway status at presentation
